newsitem.title: USA: Loews sees tobacco pact impact.
newsitem.headline: Loews sees tobacco pact impact.

text.p: Loews Corp, which owns Lorillard Tobacco Co, said a proposed litigation settlement reached between the tobacco industry and state attorney generals last week would have a material impact on its financial position if enacted.

"The company believes that implementation of the proposal would materially adversely affect its consolidated results of operations and financial position," Loews said in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing made Tuesday.

Loews' latest disclosure comes as RJR Nabisco Holdings, which owns R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, said in an SEC filing that it expects its initial payment under a recently reached tobacco accord will be $600 million, surprising analysts who thought the number would be much higher.
Philip Morris Cos. Inc. also filed with the SEC but did not estimate what its portion of the payment would be. Analyst estimates of its share range from $6.7 billion to $7 billion.

Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc, the parent of the No. 3 U.S. cigarette maker, Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., will pay an estimated $1.7 billion, leaving the balance of the $10 billion to come from Loews and UST Inc.
The agreement would require cigarette companies to pay $368.5 billion over 25 years to compensate states and smokers and to fund programs to help people quit smoking.
Of that total, tobacco companies would be required to make an initial $10 billion payment under the agreement and multibillion-dollar annual payments thereafter.

The deal also sets goals of reducing teen smoking by 42 percent in five years, 58 percent in seven years and 67 percent in 10 years or cigarette companies would be penalized by as much as $2 billion a year.
